body: Thanks for the investigation! I agree this is strange; I can't get the `formResetCallback` in your example to run in any browser despite the spec which seems to call for its invocation during construction. I'm wondering if this is really just a bug in all implementations or if there is a subtle part of the spec that excludes the callback from being run in this case. @mfreed7, any chance you know?

> I'm wondering if this is really just a bug in all implementations or if there is a subtle part of the spec that excludes the callback from being run in this case. [@mfreed7](https://github.com/mfreed7), any chance you know?

Interesting - I can confirm. That does sound like a correct reading of the spec, but it doesn't seem to be implemented. Unfortunately, I don't know the history here, so I don't know if that's a spec accident or a browser accident. I'm also wondering if it would be web compatible to just start calling `formResetCallback` every time we parse a FACE? Feels like potentially no?

There is a suspicion why implementations do not do this.

If you look at the [upgrade an element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#concept-upgrade-an-element) algorithm, you will see that step 9  enqueues some reactions related to the [form-associated custom element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#form-associated-custom-element):
> 9. If element is a [form-associated custom element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#form-associated-custom-element), then:
>
>    1. [Reset the form owner](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#reset-the-form-owner) of element. If element is associated with a [form](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/forms.html#the-form-element) element, then [enqueue a custom element callback reaction](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction) with element, callback name "formAssociatedCallback", and « the associated [form](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/forms.html#the-form-element) ».
>
>    2. If element is [disabled](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#concept-fe-disabled), then [enqueue a custom element callback reaction](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction) with element, callback name "formDisabledCallback" and « true ».

But note there is no reaction related to the `formResetCallback`.

Therefore, I guess that for consistency with [upgrade an element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#concept-upgrade-an-element), the reaction with `formResetCallback` is also not enqueue in the [create an element for a token](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#create-an-element-for-the-token) algorithm in the step 13:
> 13. If element is a [resettable element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/forms.html#category-reset), invoke its [reset algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#concept-form-reset-control). (This initializes the element's [value](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#concept-fe-value) and [checkedness](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#concept-fe-checked) based on the element's attributes.)

As I think, it seems to me that either `formResetCallback` should be added to the [upgrade an element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#concept-upgrade-an-element) algorithm or modified in the [create an element for a token](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#create-an-element-for-the-token) in the step 13, where it will be indicated that [reset algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#concept-form-reset-control) is not called for the [form-associated custom element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#form-associated-custom-element).

Opinion? @domfarolino @mfreed7

> The third case also does not execute the `formResetCallback` hook, the conditions for its execution are unachievable (due with form-associated custom elements).

Why can't these conditions be satisfied for form-associated custom elements?

----

Regardless, I think I agree with the proposal at the bottom of https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10927#issuecomment-2618404085. I've created https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11122 to address this, and I'll check out the testing story for this now.

The more I look at the test @dSalieri linked to, I'm pretty sure https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/custom-elements/form-associated/form-reset-callback.html#L52 asserts what we want: that FACE reset callbacks are not run during "create an element for a token" (which I believe is run during `insertAdjecentHTML`. So maybe we're good here on tests.

> Why can't these conditions be satisfied for form-associated custom elements?

In document [reactivation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#reactivate-a-document), the first step should be to call [reset algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#concept-form-reset-control) for all elements in the document that have an [autofill field name](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#autofill-field-name) field with the value "**off**"

For example, such a condition would correspond to an input element with an autocomplete attribute that would have the value "**off**".

Calling [reset algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#concept-form-reset-control) in [reactivation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#reactivate-a-document) should trigger a call to **formResetCallback**, but... if you look at the text of the specification, the [customized built-in element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#customized-built-in-element) is not defined as a [form-associated custom element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#custom-elements-core-concepts:concept-custom-element-definition-form-associated). Therefore, the [reset algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#concept-form-reset-control) is called for the element itself (in this case, the input element) and the **formResetCallback** hook will not be called.

Here are the texts of the specification that say all this:
> An [autonomous custom element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#autonomous-custom-element) is called a form-associated custom element if the element is associated with a [custom element definition](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#custom-element-definition) whose [form-associated](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-custom-element-definition-form-associated) field is set to true.

> **Resettable elements**
> Denotes elements that can be affected when a [form](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-form-element) element is [reset](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-form-reset).
> - [input](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-input-element), [output](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-output-element), [select](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-select-element), [textarea](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-textarea-element), [form-associated custom elements](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-associated-custom-element)

From which it follows that [customized built-in elements](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#customized-built-in-element) do not call **formResetCallback**, for this you need to be a [form-associated custom element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#custom-elements-core-concepts:concept-custom-element-definition-form-associated).

---

As for the test, I don't think it was written with the problem I'm describing in mind (but maybe I'm wrong). But yeah, it looks like it wants to say that **formResetCallback** shouldn't be called when parsing.

@domfarolino
